Corn crib bin (room 14) built in parts/room-14.mjs: a hay-bale corn heap at the back end (z 14..15) with a standing lantern on top (74,5,15); z 10..13 stay clear from the hatch.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the room line shows 4 placed, no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE. On a test copy with the crib shell added, the room check says OK: light min 8, 0 dark cells, FIT OK.
Still open: the hatch at (74,3..4,9) has no approach from the yard in the plan, so the walk from the building entrance cannot reach the bin (see left).
left: The crib's hatch (74,3..4,9) sits 2 above the yard with no approach in the plan (no ladder, dock or ramp). `mcd room` from the building entrance reports 'no way in' for the bin, so the openings/grounds part must add an approach (I noted it in plan.md Notes).

The real build has no crib shell yet (shell-b is a stub in this copy), so the room check could only run on a test copy: /tmp/part20-test/test.nbt with the bin's floor and slat walls added by hand, and the entrance moved to (74,3,10). On that copy the verdict is OK, with light min 8 and 0 dark cells, and the walk reaches 5 of 6 floor cells (the 6th is the lantern's top, not a real stand).

The corn is hay_block: the palette has no corn block, so the ears read as a hay heap, and the bin has no furniture beyond that and the lantern (it is one cell wide, so nothing else fits without blocking the way in).

waste.what: Wrote a throwaway shell (floor, slat walls, hatch air) by hand in /tmp/part20-test/shell-test.mjs so the room check had a floor to walk, because shell-b is a stub in this copy.
waste.cost: one script, ~25 block writes, two check runs and one retry on the entrance cell
waste.tool: A `mcd room --with-shell <part>` option, or a `--from-merged` flag that merges a named part's shell from the plan, would have let the room check run without a hand-written shell.

waste.what: Checked the walk by hand-moving the entrance in a copied rooms.json to test reachability from inside the bin.
waste.cost: one temp rooms.json and two runs
waste.tool: `mcd room --start x,y,z` (walk from a given cell instead of the building entrance) would have answered the reachability question directly.

waste.what: Worked out the light level at the feet for the lantern position by hand (Manhattan distance from the source).
waste.tool: `mcd light` on the test copy, which I ran only after the fact; running it first would have skipped the hand calculation.
